resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and firelookout.com date the first lookout to 1925, a cupola cabin. The 1918-1931 newspaper items show a summer lookout on the peak from 1918, so the sources disagree about the start of staffing. The Register's first lookout, named Richards, does not appear in those items.

notes_for_editor: Early history is disputed. The Register and firelookout.com give a 1925 cupola; the newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page show Denver Laughlin as summer lookout from 1918 and say he had been there nearly 15 years by 1931. I did not check the newspapers themselves. The Register's first lookout, 'Richards', is not named in those items. The record's kind 'two_story' and material 'wood' are not supported by any page I read, which describe an R-6 flattop cab on a concrete block base; left unchanged, flagged for review. The record's height_m 3.0 matches the 10-foot base (about 3.05 m) rather than a full structure height; kept at 3.0 with this caveat. Access and climbing status are not in any source, so no access facts were given. The record's photos (firelookout.com, Pete Molenda and Gary Weber) were not re-checked and no new photos were found. No web search used for this tower.
